source: Reconstructed for this dashboard from: IMF World Revenue Longitudinal Database (fiscal); V-Dem v13 and the Fraser Institute (legal, peace); World Bank WDI, WHO and Penn World Table (collective); and the Besley & Persson Pillars 2 replication archive (civil-war / repression context).
citation: Besley, Timothy and Torsten Persson. 2011. Pillars of Prosperity: The Political Economics of Development Clusters. Princeton University Press; and Besley, Persson & Dann (2021), 'Pillars of Prosperity: A Ten-Year Update', CEPR DP16256.
framework: Besley & Persson argue prosperity rests on Adam Smith's two drivers — state capacity and peace. State capacity has three dimensions: fiscal (raising revenue), legal (protecting property & contracts) and collective (delivering public goods). With peace, these are the four Pillars of Prosperity shown here.
normalization: Each pillar is scored as a WITHIN-YEAR PERCENTILE (0-100): a country's rank, among all countries with data that year, on the pillar's signal. This mirrors B-P's own method — they normalise every component relative to the cross-section of countries in each snapshot year (min-max and rank within year, then per-year PCA). Percentile rank is their Doing Business normalisation, robust to outliers across a long panel. The composite is the average of all four pillar percentiles, drawn only where all four are observed (the full-framework window, ~1980-2016, bounded by fiscal coverage from 1980 and B-P's peace metric to 2016). Native-unit values for every underlying indicator are available beneath each pillar.

pillars.label: Fiscal capacity
pillars.signal: Income-tax share of total tax revenue
pillars.description: The state's ability to raise revenue from hard-to-tax bases. Besley & Persson treat the income-tax share of total tax as the signature of fiscal capacity — income taxation requires registries, monitoring and compliance, whereas trade taxes are the 'easy' base a low-capacity state falls back on. Source: IMF World Revenue Longitudinal Database (WoRLD), 1980-2024.

indicators.label: Income-tax share of total tax
indicators.description: Income, profit & capital-gains taxes as a share of total tax revenue. B-P's fiscal-capacity signal.

indicators.label: Tax revenue (% of GDP)
indicators.description: Total tax revenue as a share of GDP — the overall reach of the fiscal system.

indicators.label: Trade-tax share of total tax
indicators.description: Taxes on international trade as a share of total tax. The 'easy' base; reliance on it signals LOW fiscal capacity.

indicators.label: Income − trade tax bias
indicators.description: Income-tax share minus trade-tax share (B-P's taxshare_bias). Higher = a more capacity-intensive tax mix.

pillars.label: Legal capacity
pillars.description: The state's ability to protect property and enforce contracts — the legal infrastructure that lets markets function. B-P's chosen annual measure is V-Dem's property-rights index; we add horizontal constraints on the executive (judicial / legislative) and the Fraser Institute's legal-structure index as convergent context.

indicators.label: Property rights (V-Dem)
indicators.description: Do citizens enjoy the right to acquire, possess, inherit and sell private property? V-Dem v2xcl_prpty, 0-1. B-P's legal-capacity signal.

indicators.label: Judicial constraints on the executive
indicators.description: The extent to which the executive respects the constitution and complies with court rulings (V-Dem v2x_jucon).

indicators.label: Legislative constraints on the executive
indicators.description: The extent to which the legislature and oversight bodies can constrain the executive (V-Dem v2xlg_legcon).

indicators.label: Legal structure & property rights (Fraser)
indicators.description: Judicial independence, impartial courts, protection of property, military non-interference and legal integrity. 0 (worst) to 10 (best).

pillars.label: Collective capacity
pillars.signal: Health + education standing (mean of life-expectancy & human-capital percentiles)
pillars.description: The state's capacity to deliver broad public goods — B-P's third, newest dimension, operationalised (after Besley & Persson 2014) as the combination of population health and education. The pillar score averages a country's within-year standing on life expectancy and human capital; schooling, infant mortality and public spending are shipped as context.

indicators.label: Life expectancy at birth
indicators.description: Life expectancy at birth, total (years). WDI. One of the two B-P collective-capacity signals.

indicators.label: Human capital index
indicators.description: PWT human-capital index built from average years of schooling and returns to education. Annual proxy for B-P's Barro-Lee schooling input.

indicators.label: Mean years of schooling (15-64)
indicators.description: Average years of total schooling for the population aged 15-64. B-P's exact education input; five-yearly.

indicators.label: Infant mortality rate
indicators.description: Infant deaths per 1,000 live births. WDI. A classic inverse marker of public-health delivery.

indicators.label: Government education spending
indicators.description: Government expenditure on education as a share of GDP — investment in collective capacity.

indicators.label: Government health spending
indicators.description: Domestic general government health expenditure as a share of GDP. WHO Global Health Expenditure DB (2000-).

pillars.label: Peace
pillars.signal: Besley-Persson peace metric — freedom from civil war & repression
pillars.description: Adam Smith's second driver and B-P's fourth pillar: the absence of political violence. This uses B-P's own metric — 0.5 x repression + civil war, scored as the cumulative share of years (from 1975) a country has avoided conflict and repression, so the value at 2016 matches their published index. Built from UCDP/PRIO civil war and their repression dummy; coverage 1975-2016. (V-Dem freedom from political killings and torture are shipped as raw context for a future, higher-coverage peace measure.)

indicators.label: Civil-war incidence (B-P score input)
indicators.description: 1 if the country was in an internal armed conflict that year (B-P's UCDP-derived war dummy). Weighted 1.0 in the peace score; inverse signal; 1946-2016.

indicators.label: Repression incidence (B-P score input)
indicators.description: 1 if the country was in a state of political repression that year (B-P repression dummy). Weighted 0.5 in the peace score; inverse signal; through 2016.

indicators.label: Freedom from political killings (V-Dem, context)
indicators.description: Freedom from political killings by the state (V-Dem v2clkill). NOT used in the current B-P peace score — shipped as context for a future, higher-coverage peace measure. Higher = freer; through 2025.

indicators.label: Freedom from torture (V-Dem, context)
indicators.description: Freedom from torture by the state (V-Dem v2cltort). NOT used in the current B-P peace score — shipped as context for a future, higher-coverage peace measure. Higher = freer; through 2025.
